description: Write a WHOLE cut into a sequence in one call — clips in order with their lengths, an optional dissolve between them, an optional bed underneath. This is the counterpart to lab_get_sequence: that one reads the timeline, this one writes it. Prefer it over a chain of lab_add_clip calls whenever you already know the whole cut: a chain that breaks in the middle leaves half a sequence behind, this either applies or refuses. Costs nothing — it validates and writes rows, it generates nothing. Every video_id is checked against the project BEFORE anything is written, so a wrong id is a refusal here and not a gap in the cut nobody notices. Pass `sequence_id` to write into THAT sequence; omit it and a new one is created. Pass `sequence_id` WITHOUT a manifest to read back the stored cut as a manifest — for an agent that already has the sequence_id and wants to see what is in there before changing it. (The Resolve bridge does NOT go through here: it talks to the FilmLab server directly with its own bridge key and does not know this MCP.) Reworking a cut you read back? Keep each clip's `clip_id`. A clip that comes back with its identity keeps its track, its in-point in the source and its scene, and the shots bound to it stay bound; a clip without one is treated as new and gets a fresh identity, which orphans whatever pointed at the old one. One honest limit: DaVinci Resolve's scripting API offers neither a transition call nor a clip volume property, so the Resolve bridge applies the clips and reports `uebergang` and the bed's level/fade as not applied. Both are stored here and are honoured by the sequence render.

erwartete_revision.description: The `revision` you read (from lab_get_sequence or this tool's read-back). The cut is written only if the sequence still has exactly that content — otherwise nothing is written and you get `revision_veraltet` with the current revision: read again, merge, write again. Without it this tool still protects the moment between its own read and write, but not the time since YOU read the sequence.

manifest.description: The cut as one object. Omit it only together with a `sequence_id`, to read back what is stored

bett.description: A bed under the whole cut. Stored on the sequence; the Resolve bridge places the clip but can set neither level nor fade

audio_id.description: Id of an audio row in this project (from lab_list_audio). Either this or url

fade_s.description: Fade in and out of the bed

pegel_db.description: Bed level relative to the clips

url.description: Direct URL of the bed. Either this or audio_id

clips.description: The cut, in cutting order. The order here IS the order on the timeline

asset_key.description: Storage key of a clip that has no video row. Either this or video_id

clip_id.description: Identity of an EXISTING clip in this sequence, as read back by this tool or by lab_get_sequence. Pass it whenever you are reworking a cut you read: the clip keeps its track, its in-point in the source and its scene, and every shot bound to it stays bound. Omit it for a clip you are adding — one is assigned

dauer_s.description: Length of this clip on the timeline. Required unless you give both in_s and out_s — a clip without a length would silently inherit the backend default, and the sequence duration and the render would drift apart

in_s.description: In point inside the source clip

out_s.description: Out point inside the source clip — must be greater than in_s

video_id.description: Id of a generated video in THIS project (from lab_list_assets). Either this or asset_key

uebergang.description: One transition kind between ALL clips. Stored on the sequence; the Resolve bridge cannot apply it

art.description: Only 'dissolve' — nothing else is implemented downstream

project_id.description: Project id (from lab_list_projects) — positive integer as string

sequence_id.description: Sequence to write into (from lab_create_sequence/lab_list_sequences). Omit to create a new one. Given WITHOUT a manifest, the stored manifest is read back instead of written

title.description: Title for the sequence created when `sequence_id` is omitted
